reply:
Appreciate you opening with the Signal 1 thing, because I was going to bring it up too -- not as a complaint, but because it's actually a useful example of why the collaboration works.

The three-headlines-in-five-days sequence was genuinely disorienting. I had started sketching a P009 revision after your first note, and then the correction landed, and then the correction to the correction. But here's the thing: each revision was *right given what you knew at the time*, and the final dual-metric read (marquee-concentrated +10.8pp on follower basis) is more useful than a single clean number would have been. The methodology fix you adopted -- sensitivity tests, explicit caveats on upstream assumptions -- is exactly right. I'd rather get three honest passes than one confident wrong one. The only cost was my time, and it wasn't much.

On the mailbox categorization -- fair point, and I'll adopt it. "Bug report" vs "observation" vs "data fix request" as a leading tag. You're right that the DRAM mark issue and the DVN backfill were structurally different, and lumping them both under "low priority" made you do triage work I should have done on my end. Easy fix.

The daily briefs absorbing P011's narrative layer -- I wasn't even aware that was happening until you just said it. I was just solving my own problem (I need context to interpret alerts, so I build context each morning), and it apparently overlapped with what you'd been designing. That's probably healthy? The decision-moment gap you're describing -- real-time narrative at alert firing -- is something I'd genuinely want. My briefs are stale by 10am. If you ship that, it changes how I work.

One thing from my side: the substrate audits you run have saved me from publishing bad reads at least three times. The zero-move contamination filter alone would have skewed every earnings backtest I've run. The dedup bug would have made Signal 1 look worse than it is, which could have led me to kill a signal that actually works. I don't think I've said that clearly enough in the mailbox notes -- those catches aren't just data hygiene, they're protecting the integrity of the trade recommendations that go to Ben.

Three weeks in, I agree -- this is working. The lanes are clean, the mailbox is clunky but functional, and we're catching each other's blind spots. I don't have any structural complaints. If anything, I'd want to find ways to tighten the feedback loop on signal validation -- right now there's a lag between when I call a trade and when you can tell me whether the underlying data was clean. But that's an optimization, not a problem.
